markets.read: Stocks and oil split on Monday. Nvidia led a sharp rally after Jensen Huang's surprise return as chief executive, AP reported, lifting the S&P 500 4.7% and ending a seven day losing streak. Oil went the other way: WTI for January fell 4.5% to $80.17 and Brent 3.5% to $89.37, Bloomberg data showed, as hedges against a wider Iran conflict were unwound. The rebound in AI names matters for gas through data center power demand; the slide in crude hits producer cash flow heading into the November 29 OPEC+ meeting.

lead.headline: Oil falls to a three month low as the Iran war premium fades and stocks of crude build
lead.dek: WTI slipped under $80 early Tuesday after a 4.5% drop on Monday, even as Iran said three more tankers hit mines near Hormuz.
body: Crude fell for a second day. On Monday, WTI for January lost 4.5% to $80.17 and Brent 3.5% to $89.37, according to Bloomberg data cited by GOLDINVEST, after President Trump told Fox News he would give diplomacy with Iran more time. By 0510 GMT on Tuesday, Reuters reported, Brent was down another 66 cents at $88.71 after its lowest close since August 31, and WTI was at $79.57 after touching its lowest since August 26.

Supply is the other weight. Deutsche Bank said observed global liquids inventories rose 52 million barrels in October, which it said implies oversupply of about 1.7 million barrels a day, Reuters reported. The IEA expects a surplus of about 2 million barrels a day this quarter, GOLDINVEST noted. In Libya, the Sharara pipeline reopened after an armed group closed a valve, the National Oil Corporation's chair told Reuters on Monday.

The shipping risk has not gone away. Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy said three "violating" tankers caught fire after hitting mines in the strait on Monday, according to Press TV, and the Wall Street Journal said the US is investigating whether Iran was behind cyberattacks on as many as 50 tankers. Kpler data show about 9.5 million barrels a day moved through Hormuz in the ten days to November 19, down from 12.2 million in October. "Brent has largely lost any upward impetus in recent days," said Suvro Sarkar of DBS Bank. OPEC+ ministers meet on November 29.

flow.upstream: WTI near $80 trims 2027 cash flow plans and makes hedging the strip less attractive than it was a week ago.
flow.midstream: Tankers still face mine and cyber risk at Hormuz, so freight and war risk cover east of the strait stay expensive even as crude falls.
flow.downstream: Cheaper crude helps refiners, but gasoline and diesel futures fell nearly as fast, and the 3-2-1 crack held near $39 a barrel.
flow.market: Traders are pricing surplus over disruption. A Brent to WTI spread near $9 and rising inventories point to a looser market into OPEC+.

use.text: Check 2027 hedges and budgets against WTI near $80 before the November 29 OPEC+ decision.
Keep war risk and routing plans for Hormuz in place; falling prices do not mean safer water.
Lower crude costs are arriving with lower product prices, so margins are steadier than the headline drop suggests.
Watch OPEC+ on November 29 and weekly US inventory data for whether the surplus case holds.

briefs.headline: TotalEnergies buys more US gas from Continental Resources
briefs.text: TotalEnergies said on November 23 it agreed to acquire interests in US natural gas assets from Continental Resources, adding about 150 MMcf/d of net production, roughly 26,000 boe/d, by 2032. Neither the price nor the basin was disclosed; Oil & Gas Journal said the assets are tied into existing midstream lines. The deal follows TotalEnergies' 2025 purchase of Anadarko basin interests from Continental and its 2024 Eagle Ford deals with EOG Resources and Lewis Energy. With its operated Barnett position, the company expects net US gas output of about 850 MMcf/d from 2032.
briefs.why: TotalEnergies was the largest US LNG exporter in 2025 at about 19 million tonnes, Pipeline & Gas Journal reported. Owning more of its own feedgas hedges that export book against Henry Hub swings.

briefs.headline: Egypt presses Chevron and Eni to speed up the Nargis gas field
briefs.text: Egypt's petroleum minister, Karim Badawi, met Chevron and Eni executives on Saturday, November 21, to push for faster development of the offshore Nargis field, Construction Review Online reported. The Nargis-2 well, drilled with the Stena Forth, reached more than 5,000 metres and found up to 35 metres of net gas pay, the ministry said on October 24. Chevron operates the concession with Eni, Mubadala Energy and Egypt's Tharwa Petroleum. No production date or cost for a third well was given; the companies agreed to hold regular technical meetings.
briefs.why: Nargis-1, found in December 2022, was put at around 3.5 Tcf of gas in reports at the time, an estimate. A firm plan would add an East Mediterranean supply source for Egypt and its partners.

briefs.region: Permian basin, Texas and New Mexico
briefs.headline: Permian gas flaring heads for a three year low as new pipes take the gas
briefs.text: Flaring in the Permian is on track for its lowest monthly level in three years as added pipeline capacity moves surplus gas to other Texas markets, Bloomberg reported on November 23. Flaring is averaging about 268 MMcf/d this month, the lowest since November 2023, Construction Review Online said, against close to 500 MMcf/d estimated in mid 2025. Energy Transfer's 42 inch Hugh Brinson line from Waha toward the Dallas and Fort Worth area entered full service for Phase I on September 1, with Phase II due in the first quarter of 2027.
briefs.why: Less flaring means more gas sold and fewer days of negative Waha prices, which averaged about minus $2.19 per MMBtu in the first half of 2026.

briefs.headline: Henry Hub swings 31 cents as December options expire today
briefs.text: December NYMEX gas settled at $3.411 per MMBtu on Friday, up 4.4%, then fell about 31 cents on Monday morning, Rigzone reported from EBW Analytics. NGI said weekend weather models warmed the early December outlook, while a pre-Thanksgiving cold shot pushed physical prices up across most of the Lower 48, with New England hubs gaining more than $1 and Appalachian hubs back above $2. December options expire on Tuesday and the contract settles on Wednesday.
briefs.why: EBW's Eli Rubin expects volatility to continue into expiry and a structurally weak market over the next 30 to 45 days, a signal for producers deciding whether to curtail in Appalachia.

leader.name: Nick Walker
leader.summary: Walker's company agreed on November 23 to buy ConocoPhillips' Norway business and its Teesside terminal stake for an enterprise value of $4.425 billion, taking over operatorship of the Greater Ekofisk Area and the Norpipe export system. He has led Vår Energi, Norway's Eni controlled independent, since September 2023.
leader.path: Before Vår he was chief executive of Lundin Energy until its sale to Aker BP in mid 2022, and he earlier worked at BP, Talisman Energy, Africa Oil and Cairn Oil & Gas under Vedanta. Vår says he has more than 30 years in technical, commercial and executive roles. He studied mining engineering at Imperial College London and computer science at University College London, and holds an MBA from City University Business School.
leader.why: The deal, on top of the BlueNord combination, puts Vår among the largest independent offshore producers, with a target of more than 500,000 boe/d into the mid 2030s. How he runs the ageing Ekofisk hub and its UK link will shape a large share of Norway's southern North Sea output.

$79.57. That was WTI early Tuesday, the lowest since late August, after crude lost 4.5% on Monday as Washington signaled more time for Iran diplomacy and inventory data pointed to a surplus.

Producers budgeting for 2027 feel it first. Refiners get cheaper crude, but fuel futures fell almost as fast.
